catalog_quote: Según la descripción de Najlis, en esta lengua el acento seria morfológicamente predecible: el acento recaería en el morfema “principal” de cada lexema; o sea en la raíz o –en el caso de compuestos- en la raíz determinante. En realidad, esto ocurre sólo en la mayoría de las palabras del selknam. Hay una cantidad de excepciones, la mayoría con probables explicaciones. Así, no tienen el acento en la primera sino en la segunda sílaba: (a) algunos elementos que son lexificaciones relativamente recientes de sintagmas originarios ... (b) algunos préstamos de la lengua yagan, que han retenido la acentuación de la lengua de origen ... (c) algunos términos de posible origen onomatopéyico ... Es posible encontrar pares mínimos, como: ′wájér ‘dispersarse’ vs. wà′jér ‘estar gritando’. En resumen, el acento es fonológicamente relevante en selknam, aun cuando en la inmensa mayoría de los lexemas sea …
sweep_summary: Selk'nam (onaa1245) is in the catalog as set by morphology (root/'morfema principal'-initial intensity stress, usually word-initial, with listed exceptions and stress minimal pairs; independent two-tone system per Najlis 1973), deciding source Viegas Barros 2015 sec. 5.1.1. this search of works with stress in the title found one title: Martini Ocampo, Alicia (1982), 'The phonology of Shelknam: the suprasegmentals', M.A. thesis SUNY Buffalo — relevant (the only dedicated study of Selk'nam word stress; it posits three phonemic stress degrees and reanalyses Najlis's tone as pitch accent, per the carried quotes in Viegas Barros fn. 213 and Rojas-Berscia p. 29 fn. 19 that the catalog already records). It is print-only: located as a physical thesis in the UB Libraries catalogue (Alma mms 990003926980204803, OCLC 09772738, 21 leaves, photocopy of typescript, no e-link); Glottolog gives a Google Books id (0-4dRAAACAAJ) but the page is blocked; nothing on archive.org, the UB repository, Crossref, or Google Books search; Priority HIGH for acquisition via ILL/scan from UB Libraries — it is the one source that could refine (secondary stress, pitch accent) or challenge the root-initial reading. Re-read of the open Najlis 1973 Rosetta Project excerpts (phoneme inventory, typological sketch, introduction) is silent on stress; Rojas-Berscia 2014 has no stress section. No new first-hand statement; catalog's classification unchanged.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim in the held Viegas Barros 2015 text at sec. 5.1.1/5.1.4 and fn. 213; locator correct modulo the already-flagged TOC/header page offset. (2) The deciding source is a 2015 comparative-historical doctoral thesis restating Najlis 1973; it is specialist, open, and internally consistent (rule = stress on first syllable of the root/'morfema principal', usually word-initial; stress minimal pairs; enumerated exception classes; tone as a separate system), and the independent held source (Rojas-Berscia 2014) does not contradict it. The primary grammar (Najlis 1973) and the only suprasegmental study (Martini Ocampo 1982) are print-only/unlocated and not yet obtained; the Rosetta Project excerpt of Najlis 1973 downloaded now (pp. 91-93) is silent on stress. No later phonology/instrumental work was found and none is expected for a language dormant since the 1970s-80s. (3) Nothin

sources.quote: No stress statement in the excerpt; it covers the 27-phoneme inventory, dialect sibilant mergers and minimal pairs, ending 'las seis vocales se oponen por zona y por tono. Las zonas son: anterior, posterior y baja. Los tonos: agudo y grave' (p. 93) — i.e. Najlis treats agudo/grave 'tone' as a vowel feature, consistent with the record's tone_note. The accent pages of Najlis 1973 are not in the Rosetta excerpts.
